target_customer: mobile app developers, marketers and publishers, especially mobile games
problem: Measuring ad spend, revenue and retention across ad networks to compute marketing ROI.
business_model: SaaS (self-service platform; a pricing page mentions US$200/month full access)

founders.name: Amir Manji
founders.background_notes: Listed as 'Head Barista' on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Integrating many ad-network APIs and processing event data at scale is standard but laborious engineering.

defensibility.rationale: SDK integration and historical data create some switching cost, but attribution was a crowded category.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: CB Insights compares Tenjin with Adjust and Flurry (undated). Tenjin stayed independent into at least 2021 (GameAnalytics partnership).

market_need_then: No dated evidence of demand was found; the 2016 funding coverage describes mobile marketers needing ROI measurement across campaigns, which is later than the 2014 founding.

brand_strength.rationale: No brand-specific press found; tenjin.com returned 503 when fetched.

outcome_analysis: Tenjin is a YC S14 mobile attribution company that raised US$2.5M in June 2016 led by NetEase Capital and kept operating for years, partnering with GameAnalytics in 2021 and still marketed as an active product in later profiles. The directory lists it as Acquired but no acquirer, date or terms was found, so the exit cannot be dated and the story is incomplete.
notes: Directory says Acquired; CB Insights also says Acquired with no buyer; no acquisition announcement found, and a 2026-dated profile describes Tenjin as operating. Possible conflict; exit.type follows the directory. Total raised: one source US$2.50M, CB Insights US$2.62M; Y Combinator, Lightbank and angels preceded the 2016 round (company-published; amounts unknown).
